text:
alex: Heads up — flipped on an adaptive token-wait policy in canary (us-east-1 / pool-gpu0). p99 for short requests dropped from ~180ms to ~95ms, p95 moved a bit too, but end-to-end throughput is down ~6% and KV cache miss rate increased ~12%.
priya: can you paste the scheduler config you used?
jamie: curious if kernel selection fell back more often because of different microbatch shapes?
alex: config pasted below — basically `max_batch_tokens` bumped to 4096 with dynamic `max_wait_ms` scaling by queue length.
```
# scheduler config (canary)
max_batch_tokens: 4096
min_batch_tokens: 32
max_wait_ms: 15  # base
adaptive_wait:
  enabled: true
  scale_by_queue_len: true
  max_scale_ms: 80
  token_thresholds: [64, 256, 1024]
```
dylan: did you sample kernel logs? want to see fallback frequency (e.g. from fast-attn kernel -> safe kernel).
alex: yes — quick snippet from runtime log around 1945678978: "kernel_fallback: fast_attn->safe_attn seq_len=128 batch_tokens=4096 reason=memory_estimate". Fallbacks are ~3.4x higher than baseline.
jamie: that explains tail: fallback path has higher latency variance and also forces KV cache recreation more often.
samira: is the KV cache key derivation stable across microbatch reorderings? we saw cache misses when requests are split across microbatches in different orders.
priya: good point — if adaptive waiting reorders by token priority we might be invalidating prefix-based cache hits. need to check request ordering invariant.
theo: proposal: try two quick experiments — A) keep max_batch_tokens high but cap adaptive max_wait to 30ms; B) reduce max_batch_tokens to 2048 and allow adaptive wait up to 80ms. measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
dylan: also add a probe to record kernel_choice per inference (fast|safe|vectorized) and kv_cache_hit boolean. store in the canary metrics for lineage.
ops-bot: deployment event: canary update by alex at 1945678920.
alex: started experiment A at 1945678945, will run for 15m then switch to B. hooking up the kernel_choice probe now.
priya: for baseline comparison include median+95/99 and tokens/sec per minute. also collect microbatch size distribution (in tokens).
jamie: anecdotal: when microbatch tokens concentrate (few large requests) mixing fast kernel with large token batches increases GPU memory pressure -> more fallbacks. we might want a small heuristic: if any single request tokens > threshold, force safe kernel proactively.
samira: noted. also check whether prefix/KV caching keys include request arrival order metadata — that would be a bug.
theo: if A gives similar p99 improvements but less throughput loss, we can keep adaptive but tweak cap. if B improves tokens/sec but p99 regresses, fallback to baseline.
dylan: do we have traces for one bad tail request? ask for top 20 p99 traces to see common pattern.
alex: collecting tail traces now; initial look shows many tails coincide with kernel fallback + KV miss + IO stall on small embeddings lookup (latency spike ~30ms).
priya: sounds like a compound effect: adaptive batching reduces latency for small requests, but increases chance of a compound slow path for mixed workloads. need smarter routing: route tiny requests to low-latency lanes (small max_batch) and large ones to throughput lanes.
ajamie: +1 — implement token-aware routing: if req.tokens <= 64 -> route to low-latency pool with small max_batch_tokens and no adaptive wait.
ops-bot: metric alert: canary kv_cache_miss_rate > baseline by 10% at 1945679050.
alex: thanks — pausing canary expansion. rolling back adaptive_wait flag on pool-gpu0. will run A/B with explicit routing instead of global adaptive.
samira: please add an experiment to tag requests with a stable cache key before any batching reordering so we can rule out cache invalidation.
theo: action items: (1) alex: re-run canary with token-aware routing + kernel_choice probe, (2) dylan: add kernel_choice+kv_hit to canary metrics, (3) priya: validate cache key invariants, (4) jamie: propose proactive kernel selection heuristic.
alex: noted, will post results after 2 runs (~2h). :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
priya: thanks — good investigation. also file a short postmortem if we expand adaptive to prod. :memo:
